=== FINDINGS FROM moonshotai_kimi-k3 ===
- README.md
  Line or code reference: lines 125-126 (the two new Variables-table rows for LEDGER_TOKENS_LOG_MAX_BYTES and LEDGER_EMIT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS); counterpart env mappings absent from .github/workflows/implement.yml (Run Codex implementation env block, lines 1777-1806; Attempt post-Codex syntax repair env block, lines 3185-3186), .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml (workflow-level env block lines 165-194 and job env lines 1305-1337), and .github/workflows/validate.yml (no LEDGER_* mapping anywhere in the file)
  Problem: Both new variables are documented in the Settings -> Secrets and variables -> Actions Variables table as operator-settable knobs used by implement, review_autofix, and validate, but no workflow YAML maps vars.LEDGER_TOKENS_LOG_MAX_BYTES or vars.LEDGER_EMIT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS into any environment, and the helper only reads its process environment (scripts/ledger_emit_substate.sh:57, :210, :253, :317). A repo-wide grep for both identifiers returns hits only in README.md, agents.md, the changelog fragment, the tests, and the helper itself.
  Why it fails at runtime: GitHub Actions never exports repository variables to the shell implicitly; they only reach a step through an explicit vars.* -> env mapping. This repo's own comments prove the convention and the failure mode: implement.yml:1797-1801 states "Repo variables are not exported to the shell on their own, so this is what makes the documented override reach the guard", and review_autofix.yml:169-171 warns "Without this export, the scripts' shell-level ${VAR:-DEFAULT} fallback fires and repo-variable overrides are silently ignored". Every comparable knob follows that pattern (CODEX_STALL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS at implement.yml:1788, review_autofix.yml:180 and :1337, orchestrate_poll.yml:692; LEDGER_SUBSTATES_ENABLED at orchestrate_poll.yml:50). An operator who sets either documented variable therefore gets no effect whatsoever: the helper sees an empty value and silently applies the compiled-in defaults (1048576 bytes / 120 seconds) at all six --tokens-log-file call sites (implement.yml:1869, implement.yml:3229, review_run_reviewers.sh:559, review_apply_fixes.sh:742, review_rb_judge.sh:242, validate_process.sh:2884, self_heal_validation.sh:137). The repo also has an established contract-test pattern for exactly this mapping (tests/test_review_autofix_review_pipeline_contract.py:2710 asserts the CODEX_STALL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS env mapping), so the fix should add the mappings plus the paired contract assertion.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4

=== FINDINGS FROM qwen_qwen3_7-plus ===
- README.md (lines 125-126) and the workflow env blocks in .github/workflows/implement.yml (around line 1789), .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml (around line 181 and 1338), and .github/workflows/validate.yml (around line 73)
  Line or code reference: README.md documents `LEDGER_TOKENS_LOG_MAX_BYTES` and `LEDGER_EMIT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` as operator-settable repo variables; scripts/ledger_emit_substate.sh reads them via `os.environ.get("LEDGER_TOKENS_LOG_MAX_BYTES")` and `os.environ.get("LEDGER_EMIT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS")`.
  Problem: Neither variable is mapped from `vars.*` into the job environment in any of the three workflow files that the README says uses them (implement, review_autofix, validate). The shell wrapper passes `${LEDGER_TOKENS_LOG_MAX_BYTES:-}` and `${LEDGER_EMIT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS:-}` into the Python heredoc, but because `vars.*` are not auto-exposed to the shell (implement.yml:56 states this explicitly), both env vars arrive empty at the Python layer and the compiled-in defaults (1048576 and 120) always apply.
  Why it fails at runtime: An operator who reads the README, sets `LEDGER_TOKENS_LOG_MAX_BYTES` or `LEDGER_EMIT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` as a repo variable, and expects the override to take effect gets no change in behavior. The helper silently uses its defaults. This is the same pattern as `CODEX_STALL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`, `CODEX_STALL_KILL_GRACE_SECONDS`, `CODEX_HEARTBEAT_ENABLED`, and `WORKSPACE_HOOK_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`, all of which are properly mapped via `${{ vars.VAR_NAME || 'default' }}` in the workflow YAML.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5

The helper's `os.environ.get(...)` calls receive empty strings and fall through to defaults.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
